goal: Make Docket's LLM layer survive a provider refusing on billing, then let a project bring its own model and key and see what it spent.

entries.title: 1. credit-hold — stop mass-failing jobs when the provider refuses on billing
entries.description:
Before specifying, read .specify/roadmaps/llm-credentials.md in full — in particular its preamble (the goal paragraph and the 'Behaviour on main that every entry builds on' bullets covering the provider layer in src/server/llm/, LlmFailureKind and its two pgEnums, the jobs runner's TEMPORARY/retryLater/fail behaviour, the env-only secrets invariant, and usage being captured but never persisted), the 'Rules for every entry' list, and this entry's own section '1. credit-hold'. Also read docs/generator.md ('Configuring a provider', 'Jobs') and docs/security.md in full, as the roadmap preamble requires of every entry.

Problem as the author verified it: credit exhaustion today permanently fails every job item it touches and points the operator at the wrong thing. Anthropic returns HTTP 400 invalid_request_error ('Your credit balance is too low...'), not 402 or 429; the SDK raises BadRequestError; src/server/llm/anthropic.ts:25-31 maps it to bad_request; that kind is absent from TEMPORARY, so runner.ts:318 calls fail(). The SDK's own maxRetries: 2 does not retry 400s. At defaults (60s worker interval, GENERATION_TICK_MAX_ITEMS=2) this permanently fails roughly 120 items per hour of outage, capped at the 500-item job limit. OpenAI differs only in shape: insufficient_quota arrives as 429 -> RateLimitError -> rate_limited, which *is* temporary, so it burns three doomed retries over about 20 minutes and then fails identically.

Build: detect billing refusal on both providers (Anthropic by inspecting the 400's message, OpenAI by insufficient_quota); give it its own persisted failure kind, which per the preamble means a migration touching both pgEnums (llm_failure_kind in src/server/db/schema/generation.ts and generation_job_item_error in src/server/db/schema/jobs.ts); and stop the runner claiming items while the credential is refusing on billing, resuming automatically when a call succeeds again. The author is explicit that merely adding the kind to TEMPORARY is NOT sufficient: three attempts over about 20 minutes still mass-fails an outage that lasts until someone tops up. Surface the held state honestly on the Batch jobs screens and name billing as the cause.

Design constraint the author imposes for the benefit of entry 2: scope the hold by credential owner from day one, even though there is exactly one credential today. Entry 2 widens that scope to per-project and must not have to rework it.

Must leave the repo working and state in its own docs what it does not do and which later entry owns it. No secret may reach a log, a response or the UI; extend the secret-scan suite (tests/integration/security/secret-scan.test.ts, tests/integration/no-plaintext.test.ts) rather than exempting it.

Does NOT: add per-project keys or settings of any kind — entry 2 (per-project-llm) owns that; persist token usage or cost — entry 3 (llm-cost-visibility) owns that; or change what happens to the already-landed operator message in src/server/llm/messages.ts, which the author marks done and explicitly not to re-spec.
entries.rationale: The author frames credit exhaustion as a recurring operational event rather than an edge case, because Docket is moving to Anthropic claude-haiku-4-5 against a shared monthly API credit pool that other work also consumes. It is first because the current behaviour silently destroys work at scale (~120 permanently failed items per hour of outage, operator told to check the wrong thing), and because its hold needs credential-owner scoping in place before entry 2 widens that scope to per-project.

entries.title: 2. per-project-llm — a project can bring its own model and API key
entries.description:
Before specifying, read .specify/roadmaps/llm-credentials.md in full — in particular its preamble (goal paragraph and the 'Behaviour on main that every entry builds on' bullets, especially the provider layer / parseLlmConfig in src/server/llm/config.ts:37 and its env vars, the env-only secrets invariant quoted from docs/generator.md, and the social-account encrypt-at-rest pattern under CREDENTIALS_ENCRYPTION_KEY), the 'Rules for every entry' list (which carries extra obligations aimed specifically at this entry), and this entry's own section '2. per-project-llm'. Also read docs/generator.md ('Configuring a provider', 'Jobs') and docs/security.md in full, as the roadmap preamble requires of every entry.

Purpose as the author states it: so a project willing to spend its own tokens can choose a more capable model than the install's default. Per-project provider, model and API key, resolved as project override falls back to the env default, so an install that sets only env vars behaves exactly as it does today.

Build: encrypted-at-rest storage reusing the CREDENTIALS_ENCRYPTION_KEY pattern that social account credentials already use; a project settings surface restricted to owner and admin for editing; a per-project equivalent of `pnpm llm:check` so someone can validate a key before trusting it with a 500-item job; redaction everywhere a key could surface. Extend entry 1's hold to per-project credential scope — one project running dry must not hold another's jobs.

Documentation obligations the author attaches to this entry specifically: it reverses the env-only key invariant that docs/generator.md states ('Keys are read from the environment only and never stored, logged or rendered'). Record that reversal in docs/decisions.md next to the generator decisions, update docs/generator.md, and say what happens to installs that only ever used env vars.

Testing/safety requirement: no secret may reach a log, a response or the UI. Both OPENAI_API_KEY and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY are already named in the secret-scan regression suite (tests/integration/security/secret-scan.test.ts, tests/integration/no-plaintext.test.ts); extend that suite to cover per-project stored keys rather than exempting anything from it.

Must leave the repo working and state what it does not do and which later entry owns it.

Does NOT: report spend or cost — entry 3 (llm-cost-visibility) owns that; add any provider beyond the existing `openai` and `anthropic`; or let a non-admin see or test a key.
entries.rationale: The author's stated reason is to let a project willing to spend its own tokens choose a more capable model than the install's default, while keeping env-only installs behaving exactly as they do today via override-falls-back-to-env resolution. It follows entry 1 so that entry 1's credential-owner-scoped hold can be widened to per-project rather than reworked.

entries.title: 3. llm-cost-visibility — show a project what it spent
entries.description:
Before specifying, read .specify/roadmaps/llm-credentials.md in full — in particular its preamble (goal paragraph and the 'Behaviour on main that every entry builds on' bullets, especially the last one: LlmUsage with inputTokens/outputTokens is returned by every call and written to the log line by logLlmCall in src/server/llm/log.ts, and no `usage` column exists anywhere in the generation schema), the 'Rules for every entry' list, and this entry's own section '3. llm-cost-visibility'. Also read docs/generator.md ('Configuring a provider', 'Jobs') and docs/security.md in full, as the roadmap preamble requires of every entry.

Sequencing the author gives: only worth building once entry 2 (per-project-llm) has projects spending their own money. LlmUsage is already returned by every call and logged, but nothing persists it, so there is no history to report.

Build: persist per-call input and output tokens against the generation that produced them, and surface per-project usage and estimated spend. Per-token prices differ by provider and model and change over time, so this spec must decide where rates live and how an unpriced model is displayed — the author's position is that an estimate labelled as one beats a confident wrong number.

Must leave the repo working and state what it does not do. No secret may reach a log, a response or the UI; extend the secret-scan suite rather than exempting it.

Does NOT: enforce budgets, cap or throttle generation on spend, or bill anyone. Reporting only. The author names no later entry owning those — this is the last entry in the roadmap, so they are simply out of scope.
entries.rationale: The author's reason is dependency and value ordering: reporting spend is only worth building once entry 2 has projects spending their own money, and there is no history to report today because usage is logged but never persisted. The 'estimate labelled as one beats a confident wrong number' line is the author's reason for forcing the spec to decide rate storage and unpriced-model display explicitly.
